    • setAutoCaptureFaceAfterValidation

      ICaptureEngineFaceConfigBuilder setAutoCaptureFaceAfterValidation(boolean value)
      sets whether the face capture will be trigger automatically when the face is validated. If false, validation will still occur, but the capture sequence is manually triggered by the user pressing a button. If true, the user can still manually trigger the capture if the auto-capture has not yet triggered. (true, by default)
      Parameters:
      value - whether the face capture will be trigger automatically when the face is validated (true, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

    • setMinFaceWidthInPixels

      ICaptureEngineFaceConfigBuilder setMinFaceWidthInPixels(int value)
      sets the minimum number of pixels wide a face must be to be 'valid'. If less than or equal to 0, this setting is ignored. If greater than 0, then the minimum will be enforced (and any setting in getMinFaceWidthToMinorImageAxisRatio() will be ignored). Default is 0
      Parameters:
      value - the minimum number of pixels wide a face must be to be 'valid' (0, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

    • setMinFaceWidthToMinorImageAxisRatio

      ICaptureEngineFaceConfigBuilder setMinFaceWidthToMinorImageAxisRatio(float value)
      sets the ratio between a captured face and the image's minor axis which determines the minimum 'valid' face size. The minor axis is the shortest dimension of the captured image. Using this value for the ratio keeps the capture consistent when capturing in landscape or portrait mode. If this value is, for example, 0.25, and the capture dimensions are 4032x3024, then the minimum face width would be 3024px * 0.25 = 756px. If this value invalid input: '<'= 0, then it is ignored. If both getMinFaceWidthToMinorImageAxisRatio() and getMinFaceWidthInPixels() are greater than 0, then this value is ignored. The default is 0.25f
      Parameters:
      value - the minimum ratio between a captured face and the image's minor axis (0.25f, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

      Parameters:
      value - the maximum number of pixels wide a face can be to be 'valid' (0, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

    • setMaxFaceWidthToMinorImageAxisRatio

      ICaptureEngineFaceConfigBuilder setMaxFaceWidthToMinorImageAxisRatio(float value)
      gets the ratio between a captured face and the image's minor axis which determines the maximum 'valid' face size. The minor axis is the shortest dimension of the captured image. Using this value for the ratio keeps the capture consistent when capturing in landscape or portrait mode. If this value is, for example, 0.75, and the capture dimensions are 4032x3024, then the minimum face width would be 3024px * 0.75 = 2268px. If this value invalid input: '<'= 0, then it is ignored. If both getMaxFaceWidthToMinorImageAxisRatio() and getMaxFaceWidthInPixels() are greater than 0, then this value is ignored. The default is 0.75f.
      Parameters:
      value - the maximum ratio between a captured face and the image's minor axis (0.75f, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

    • setRequiredMillisecondsOfValidFacesBeforeCapture

      ICaptureEngineFaceConfigBuilder setRequiredMillisecondsOfValidFacesBeforeCapture(int value)
      gets the milliseconds of consecutive validated faces that must be acquired in order to trigger auto capture. If auto capture is disabled, then validation still occurs, and the user we be notified they should manually trigger the capture. The user can manually trigger the capture before this requirement is met. This requirement is based on a timeframe and not number of times an actual captured face is validated. This is to make the capture sequence feel the same across devices. This timeframe should be long enough to ensure that an adequate number of faces are validated on lower end devices. The default value is 1500.
      Parameters:
      value - the milliseconds of consecutive validated faces that must be acquired in order to trigger auto capture (1500, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

    • setFaceExportPaddingFactor

      ICaptureEngineFaceConfigBuilder setFaceExportPaddingFactor(float value)
      gets the factor used to expand a captured face's width for exporting purposes. The face capture process is tightly bound to the dimensions of the captured face. This setting allows the width of the bounding box of the face to be padded by multiplying the width of the face by a factor when exporting a cropped image of the face. This is also used when displaying the captured face in the review capture view. This is used in tandem with getFaceExportHeightToWidthFactor(). Default value is 1.5f, so if the getFaceExportPaddingFactor() is 1.5f, and the real face width is 100px, then the width of the exported face would be 100px*1.5=150px
      Parameters:
      value - the factor used to expand the width of a captured face for exporting purposes (1.5f, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

    • setFaceExportHeightToWidthFactor

      ICaptureEngineFaceConfigBuilder setFaceExportHeightToWidthFactor(float value)
      gets the factor used to expand a captured face's height for exporting purposes. The face capture process is tightly bound to the dimensions of the captured face. This setting allows the height of the bounding box of the face to be padded by multiplying the padded width of the face by a factor when exporting a cropped image of the face. This is also used when displaying the captured face in the review capture view. This is used in tandem with getFaceExportPaddingFactor(). Default value is 1.0f, so if the getFaceExportPaddingFactor() is 1.5f, and the real face width is 100px, then the width of the exported face would be 100px*1.5=150px and the height of the exported face would be 1.0*(100px*1.5)=150px.
      Parameters:
      value - the factor used to expand the height of a captured face for exporting purposes (1.0f, by default)
      Returns:
      the builder

      sets whether to show face detection overlays during capture for debug purposes. This will show the realtime detection of the face during the capture preview. This is 'false' by default, and should only be used for debugging purposes.
      Parameters:
